name: claude-skills
description: A collection of Claude Code skills and plugins.

plugins.name: data-analysis-review
plugins.description: Empirical, objective review of a data science project: independently re-derives findings from raw data and code, then checks whether the project's own stated conclusions hold up. All analysis -- including code execution -- runs against a disposable copy of the project, so the original is never modified.

plugins.name: ciso
plugins.description: Organizes work toward security certifications (HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and CMMC) alongside the development work that satisfies them. Action-oriented verbs -- register, interview, review a PR, attach evidence, audit readiness -- tracked via persistent local HTML dashboards, an index across every supported certification plus one page each. Ships structural control metadata, plus verbatim requirement text only where the publisher's work carries no copyright (CMMC's NIST and eCFR sources); licensed requirement wording is imported per-org at runtime and never stored in this repo.

plugins.name: docs-warden
plugins.description: Keeps repository documentation consistent and honest. Scaffolds a universal document set scaled by repo archetype, audits existing repos for missing, stale, or off-standard docs, enforces append-only architecture decision records, offers to archive the oldest of them into a digest once fifty are decided, and regenerates the generated ones so drift from the code is reported rather than discovered. Ships a plain-English Vale style alongside it, and a domain-model skill that maps a repo's concepts, their relationships, and which document describes each, in Python, JS/TS, PowerShell and Terraform, plus optional compliance overlays for IEC 62304, the OSPS Baseline, the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIST SSDF, each describing document structure only and never inventing regulatory content.

plugins.name: fabflows
plugins.description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped worker agents -- explorer and researcher on Haiku, editor and test-runner on Sonnet, refuter and investigator on Opus -- and makes the lead re-verify what they report instead of trusting it. Adds fabflows:build, a deterministic loop in which an Opus builder implements a spec and a fresh reviewer returns ACCEPT or REWORK. Ships an ACTIVE guard hook that asks the user before package installs and package runners such as npx, and denies them in workers (one exception: pypdf into a literal scratchpad --target with --isolated), and blocks commits and pushes to a default branch, destructive shell commands, and reads or writes of credential files, and destructive commands written into a Makefile, npm script or shell script; the guard fails open, so a bug degrades to no guard rather than a blocked session. The using-fabflows skill is the session entrypoint and standing opt-in to the build loop. The brainstorming skill turns a rough idea into a spec the build loop can take: the lead asks bounded rounds of questions with recommended answers, workers read the codebase and the web, and the refuter attacks the draft lens by lens before the spec is written. The fabflows-setup skill points the repository at a tracker (GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear) in a committed .claude/fabflows.json; the spec then lives in the linked ticket instead of docs/specs/, the ticket skill keeps that ticket current through its MCP tools and, at the start of a new session, reminds Claude to close tickets, or to ask before cancelling them, when their PR merged or closed outside the session, and the ticket.js hook requires Refs and Spec trailers on commits and the key in the PR title. The trace skill writes an audit trace report outside the repo: every merged change with its PR approvers, ticket, approved spec hash, Compliance section and flags such as no-ticket or self-approved.
